root_cause.text: In the kexec/IMA path, kimage_map_segment() incorrectly assumed every kexec segment had IND_SOURCE-backed source pages to vmap(), but CMA-allocated segments created by contiguous allocation have no IND_SOURCE page list and must be accessed via the CMA page directly.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that after 07d24902977e, “there is no IND_SOURCE for the kexec segment” when allocated in CMA, yet “the current implementation of kimage_map_segment() assumes that IND_SOURCE pages exist and map them into a contiguous virtual address by vmap()”; the patch fixes this by checking image->segment_cma[idx] and returning page_address(cma) instead of using vmap().

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle CMA-backed kimage segments by returning the CMA page address directly instead of mapping them through the normal segment path.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `struct page *cma` is introduced in `kimage_map_segment()`, assigned from `image->segment_cma[idx]`, and an early-return path is added so that if this pointer is non-NULL the function immediately returns `page_address(cma)` before executing the existing address/size setup and page collection logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, segments backed by a CMA page now bypass the normal source-page collection and contiguous virtual mapping path, and instead directly use the virtual address of the stored CMA page. This enables correct handling of CMA-backed segments and avoids unnecessarily processing them through the generic mapping flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a vmalloc-address check before calling vunmap() in kimage_unmap_segment() to avoid invalid unmapping of non-vmalloc buffers.
intent_record.what: The function kimage_unmap_segment() was changed from unconditionally calling vunmap(segment_buffer) to first checking is_vmalloc_addr(segment_buffer), and only calling vunmap(segment_buffer) when that check is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents vunmap() from being invoked on addresses that are not vmalloc-backed mappings, avoiding invalid unmap operations when segment_buffer does not refer to vmalloc memory while preserving existing behavior for vmalloc-mapped buffers.

grouping_result.intent: Handle CMA-backed kimage segments by returning the CMA page address directly instead of mapping them through the normal segment path.
Add a vmalloc-address check before calling vunmap() in kimage_unmap_segment() to avoid invalid unmapping of non-vmalloc buffers.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by special-casing CMA-backed kexec segments, avoiding the incorrect assumption that all segments have IND_SOURCE-backed pages to vmap and instead using the CMA page address directly.

The vulnerability is about incorrect assumptions in kexec segment mapping/unmapping for CMA-backed segments versus vmalloc/vmap-backed ones. Adding a vmalloc-address check before vunmap() directly addresses the same root cause by preventing unmapping of buffers that were not vmap()'d, such as CMA-backed segment mappings.

candidates.rationale: CMA-backed segments are returned as direct page addresses rather than vmalloc/vmap addresses. Unconditionally calling vunmap() on such a buffer causes invalid unmapping, directly reflecting the bad assumption that all mapped segments came from vmap.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the vulnerable mapping operation in kimage_map_segment(). It unconditionally vmaps src_pages, assuming every kexec segment has an IND_SOURCE-backed source page list. CMA-allocated segments do not have such a list and must instead be accessed through the CMA page directly, making this statement the core of the incorrect assumption described in the root cause.

This unconditional unmap in kimage_unmap_segment() reflects the same faulty assumption that segment buffers always come from vmap(). For CMA-backed segments, the returned buffer is a direct page address rather than a vmalloc/vmap address, so calling vunmap() on it is invalid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it fully shows how kimage_map_segment() gathers pages to map. The vulnerable construct is present: the code only collects pages when it sees `entry & IND_SOURCE` and then uses `src_page_addr = entry & PAGE_MASK; src_pages[i++] = virt_to_page(__va(src_page_addr));`. This matches the root cause that the implementation assumes every segment has IND_SOURCE-backed source pages. There is no alternative handling for CMA-allocated segments that do not have an IND_SOURCE page list and must instead be accessed via the CMA page directly. The loop logic `if (entry & IND_DESTINATION) ... else if (entry & IND_SOURCE) ...` means non-IND_SOURCE segments are ignored for page collection, and the later `WARN_ON(i < npages); vaddr = vmap(src_pages, npages, VM_MAP, PAGE_KERNEL);` shows it proceeds based on that assumption rather than correctly handling CMA-backed segments. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
